title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the halting pattern, the left-going pass over a block and the two crossings of the block of 111110 words for every length. A halt needs a pass that reaches a lone 1 at the left end of the tape (given the observed fact that 0s inside the tape are single). The last pass to reach the left end did so at step 143,858,957 and did not halt; none has come within 65 cells of it since, in a reduced system followed to trigger 1,073,741,824.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The halting pattern
claims.text: 0 0 1 D> 0, the pass on the separator right of a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left, halts three steps later (F reads 0). By the table this is the only way to halt after the first step (hand argument in the README).

claims.title: The pass
claims.text: Moving left from separator to separator, the pass cuts a block of length k+3 into k+1 and 1 and goes on (pass_split); a block of length 1 stops it (pass_stop). For all lengths and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: Crossing the block of words does not depend on its length
claims.text: The pass crosses n words 111110 in 6n steps, in the same state, turning each into 1110 10; the sweep back turns them into 111110 again. For every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>11</sup> steps; the arrivals at the left end
claims.text: The real machine runs 10<sup>11</sup> steps without a halt. Passes reached the left end of the tape at triggers 1, 4, 7, 12, 18, 24, 45, 2384 and 8520 (step 143,858,957). At the last one the zone started again at the right end and a block of about 2,820 words stayed behind.

claims.title: The reduced system
claims.text: With the growing block cut to 10 words at every trigger (which, by the two crossings, should not change the rest of the tape; checked against the real machine on 20,000 triggers, not proved), the run from trigger 20,000 to 1,073,741,824 has no halt and no arrival at the left end; the deepest pass came within 65 cells of it.

claims.title: The leftmost zone alone
claims.text: The leftmost zone run by itself, one arriving pass at a time, from the real configuration of trigger 100, reproduces the real arrival of trigger 8520 (same new cells, same blocks afterwards). Continued, this model halts in its tick 4,581,101 after 19 more arrivals. That is not a prediction for the machine: after trigger 8520 the old zone gets a pass only when the new zone lets one through (32 of them by trigger 5,165,364, fewer than 64 by trigger 3·10<sup>8</sup>; the model needs about 4.6 million), and the block between the two zones is being used up, which the model does not describe.

claims.title: Halting needs the left end
claims.text: At the snapshots taken the 0s inside the tape are single, so the halting pattern can only form at the leftmost block. Observed, not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts if a pass reaches the leftmost block while that block is a lone 1 with blank tape on its left; nothing known forces or forbids that.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD1RB_1LF0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A zone of about a hundred cells is rewritten again and again by passes coming from the right, where a block of 111110 words keeps growing. The machine stops only if a pass gets through the whole zone and finds a lone 1 at the very left end of the tape. The last pass to get there did so at step 143,858,957 and did not stop the machine.

facts.text: The halting pattern: a pass meets a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left.
Crossing the block of words is proved not to depend on its length.
No halt; the last arrival at the left end was at step 143,858,957.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.605).
After 109 steps the tape spans 58,407 cells (19 left of the start, 45,037 right), with a density of 1s of 0.733.

sections.heading: A counter beside a growing block
html: The tape is a row of blocks of 1s with single 0s between them. At the right end a block of words 111110 grows by two cells per round trip of the head. Left of it is a zone of about a hundred cells that every round trip rewrites.

A round trip starts at the right end. The pass runs left in state D: it crosses the words (each becomes 1110 10), and in the zone it cuts every block of three or more 1s into two, until it meets a block of length 1, where it stops. The head then sweeps back, restoring the words. How deep the passes get behaves like a counter: deeper passes are rarer and rarer.

The machine halts only on 0 0 1 D> 0: the pass finds a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left. Inside the tape the 0s are single (observed), so this needs a pass that gets through the whole zone and finds a lone 1 at the very left end of the tape.

Passes reached the left end at triggers 1, 4, 7, 12, 18, 24, 45, 2384 and 8520 (a trigger is a new cell on the right in state B). At the last one, step 143,858,957, the zone started again at the right end; the block of about 2,820 words it had built stayed behind, between the new zone and the old one. The old zone now moves only when the new one overflows.

Cutting the growing block short should not change the rest of the tape, because Lean proves that crossing it does not depend on its length. That reduction is checked on 20,000 triggers but not proved. The reduced run, followed to trigger 1,073,741,824, has no halt and no new arrival at the left end.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: Counter zone beside a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a lone 1 at the left end of the tape
summary: A zone of about a hundred cells is rewritten like a counter by passes coming from a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a pass that reaches a lone 1 at the left end of the tape. The last arrival at the left end was at step 143,858,957; no halt in 10^11 steps.
